taxonomyNote: CWHR places Thamnophis in Natricidae while NatureServe uses Colubridae; NatureServe notes atratus, hydrophilus and aquaticus were formerly treated as subspecies of T. couchii, and Wikipedia recognizes three subspecies.
fieldMarks: Slender garter snake 46-102 cm long whose colour varies: pale gray with alternating rows of darker side blotches, dark brown with less distinct borders, or nearly all black.
Yellow dorsal stripe may be present, confined to the neck, very indistinct or absent; throat and belly whitish to yellow.
One morph is blue-gray with a faint olive dorsal stripe and white dots along the sides; another has a yellow stripe and black side spots.
Closely tied to streams: basks on streamside rocks and banks and retreats into the water.
behavior: Active diurnal snake that basks on streamside rocks or vegetation and flees rapidly into the water when disturbed.
Forages in and along streams for fish (especially trout and sculpins), tadpoles, frogs, salamanders and their larvae; also leeches and earthworms.
May be active in any month but is most often found April-July; mates in spring and gives birth to live young, August-October, in secluded sites such as under bark.
Seeks cover under water beneath rocks or among exposed tree roots.
habitat: Rocky fast-flowing streams, sluggish soft-bottomed streams, ponds, small lakes and adjacent riparian zone, within woodlands, woodland-grass edges or chaparral; usually tied closely to water but sometimes travels on land.
range: Southwestern Oregon and western California north of Point Conception (Coast Ranges from the Oregon border to central Santa Barbara County), from sea level to about 1,920 m; absent from the Salinas Valley. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Sierra gartersnake (Thamnophis couchii)
lookalikes.howToTell: Distinguished mainly by range: Sierra gartersnake is the Sierra Nevada species, aquatic gartersnake the Coast Ranges species; both were once lumped as T. couchii.

lookalikes.name: Terrestrial gartersnake (Thamnophis elegans)
lookalikes.howToTell: Formally distinct species (Rossman and Stewart 1987); aquatic gartersnake forages almost entirely in and along streams, terrestrial also occurs in deserts, meadows and forests.
